title: Splitting an integral monoid over a finite free sharpening group, allowing torsion units
statement:
Let $R$ be an integral commutative monoid, written additively: its canonical map to its group completion $G=R^{\rm gp}$ is injective [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Regard $R$ as a submonoid of $G$, put $U=R^\times=\{r\in R:-r\in R\}$, and let $B=R/U$ be the quotient identifying elements whose difference in $G$ belongs to $U$. Let $q:R\to B$ be the quotient map. Assume $B^{\rm gp}$ is a free abelian group of finite rank, meaning it has a finite basis over $\mathbf Z$. Then the canonical map $B\to B^{\rm gp}$ is injective, the induced homomorphism $\pi:G\to B^{\rm gp}$ is surjective with kernel $U$, and there is a group homomorphism $t:B^{\rm gp}\to G$ such that $\pi t=\mathrm{id}$ and $t(B)\subseteq R$. Writing $j=t|_B:B\to R$, one has $qj=\mathrm{id}_B$, and the maps
$$B\oplus U\longrightarrow R,\quad (b,u)\longmapsto j(b)+u,\qquad R\longrightarrow B\oplus U,\quad r\longmapsto(q(r),r-j(q(r)))$$
are inverse monoid isomorphisms. Here the direct sum is the Cartesian product with componentwise addition. No finite generation of $R$, saturation of $R$, or torsion-freeness of $G$ or $U$ is assumed.

source.place: Expose VI, 3.7(a), printed p. 75, splitting the exact sequence (3.a) and restricting its group section to the sharp monoid; Expose VIII, 3.1.1--3.1.2, printed p. 98. Agent algebraic generalization of old sharp-chart step 3, with possibly torsion units.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-integral-sharpening-group-exactness] to the integral monoid $R$, with $G=R^{\rm gp}$, $U=R^\times$ and the quotient $q:R\to B=R/U$; its quotient relation (elements differing by addition of a unit) is the relation of the statement, since $r-s\in U$ means $r=s+u$ with $u\in U$. It gives that $U$ is a subgroup of $G$, that $q(r)\mapsto r+U$ is an injective monoid homomorphism $B\to G/U$, hence that $B$ is integral, i.e. the canonical map $i:B\to B^{\rm gp}$ is injective, and that the induced homomorphism $\pi:G\to B^{\rm gp}$, $r-s\mapsto i(q(r))-i(q(s))$, is surjective with $\ker\pi=U$. These are the first three assertions of the statement.

source.place: Expose VI, 3.7(a), exact sequence (3.a) and its section, printed p. 75; Expose VIII, 3.1.1--3.1.2, printed p. 98. Explicit elementary algebraic generalization.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-group-section-monoid-product] with $P=R$, $Q=B$ and the quotient map $q$, which is a surjective monoid homomorphism because every class has a representative. Its hypotheses hold: $R$ is integral by assumption and $B$ is integral by step 1; the induced $\pi:G\to B^{\rm gp}$ is surjective with kernel $U=R^\times$ by step 1; and $H=B^{\rm gp}$ has the finite $\mathbf Z$-basis assumed in the statement, rank $0$ allowed. It supplies a group homomorphism $t:B^{\rm gp}\to G$ with $\pi t=\mathrm{id}$ and $t(B)\subseteq R$, its restriction $j:B\to R$ with $qj=\mathrm{id}_B$, and the inverse monoid isomorphisms $F(b,u)=j(b)+u$ and $E(r)=(q(r),r-j(q(r)))$ between $B\oplus U$ (Cartesian product with componentwise addition) and $R$.

proof.text: The maps $F$ and $E$ of step 2 are exactly the two displayed maps of the statement, and $j=t|_B$. Together with step 1 this gives every assertion. No finite generation or saturation of $R$ and no torsion-freeness of $G$ or $U$ is assumed in [lem-trf-integral-sharpening-group-exactness] or [lem-trf-group-section-monoid-product], so none is used.
